title: NHS Struggles: From Maternity Safety to Emergency Room Delays
subtitle: As the government works to fix crumbling maternity units, patients face long waits and poor conditions in emergency departments.

summary.en: The UK government is facing significant pressure to improve NHS services across the country. Recent reports show that nearly half of maternity units in England do not meet basic safety standards. Meanwhile, in Wales, a new plan aims to stop the practice of treating patients in hospital corridors by 2029. Patients have shared stories of waiting for days in emergency departments due to system-wide pressures. Officials acknowledge that current conditions are unacceptable and require urgent national attention.
summary.zh: 英國政府正面臨改善全國國家醫療保健服務（NHS）的巨大壓力。最新報告顯示，英格蘭近半數的產科單位未達基本安全標準。與此同時，威爾斯提出一項新計畫，目標在 2029 年前終結在醫院走廊治療病患的現象。病患紛紛分享因體系壓力而在急診室等待數日的經歷。官員承認目前的狀況令人無法接受，亟需全國關注。

paragraphs.en: The National Health Service (NHS) is facing a difficult period as it struggles to manage safety and efficiency across its hospitals. Following recent concerns about the condition of maternity units, new reports highlight that the challenges extend deep into emergency care. While the government works to address failing hospital buildings, patients are also speaking out about long and uncomfortable waits in emergency departments.
paragraphs.zh: 英國國家醫療保健服務（NHS）正處於艱難時期，致力於管理旗下醫院的安全與效率。繼近期對產科單位狀況的擔憂後，最新報告指出，這些挑戰已深入影響到急診照護。在政府努力修繕老舊醫院建築的同時，病患也紛紛發聲，抱怨在急診室面臨漫長且不適的等待。

paragraphs.en: In November 2026, concerns grew after the government admitted it could not yet estimate the cost of repairing failing maternity and neonatal units. These units provide care for newborn babies. According to previous reports, nearly half of these facilities in England currently fail to meet basic safety standards. Poor building conditions have created an environment where staff struggle to provide the high level of care that patients expect and deserve.
paragraphs.zh: 2026 年 11 月，政府承認尚無法估算修繕產科與新生兒病房所需的費用，引發各界擔憂。這些單位負責照護新生兒。根據先前的報告，英格蘭目前有近半數的相關設施未達基本安全標準。惡劣的建築條件導致醫護人員難以提供病患所期待且應得的高品質照護。

paragraphs.en: These infrastructure problems are now being matched by serious issues in emergency care. In Wales, the government has announced a new £23 million plan to end the practice of “corridor care” by 2029. Corridor care happens when hospitals are so full that they must treat patients in hallways or other spaces not designed for medical care. Senior emergency doctors have warned that this practice is dangerous and that too many patients are having a terrible experience while waiting for help.
paragraphs.zh: 這些基礎設施問題如今與急診照護的嚴重缺失相呼應。威爾斯政府已宣布一項 2300 萬英鎊的新計畫，目標在 2029 年前終結「走廊醫療」的現象。所謂走廊醫療，是指醫院因過度擁擠，被迫將病患安置在走廊或其他非醫療設計的空間進行治療。資深急診醫師警告，這種做法相當危險，且已有太多病患在等待救治的過程中經歷了極其糟糕的對待。

paragraphs.en: One patient, 63-year-old Andrew Railton, shared his difficult experience at the Royal Glamorgan Hospital. Mr. Railton reported that he spent more than 50 hours sitting in a chair in a corridor during two separate visits. He was being treated for pneumonia and low potassium levels, a condition where the body lacks an important mineral. He described the experience as “something Victorian,” noting that he was forced to wait in a draughty hallway while receiving treatment through a drip. The local health board apologized, admitting that his experience fell below the standards the NHS aims to provide.
paragraphs.zh: 63 歲的病患安德魯·瑞爾頓（Andrew Railton）分享了他在皇家格拉摩根醫院（Royal Glamorgan Hospital）的艱難經歷。瑞爾頓先生表示，他在兩次就診期間，總計有超過 50 小時坐在走廊的椅子上。當時他因肺炎及鉀離子濃度過低（一種體內缺乏重要礦物質的病症）接受治療。他形容這種體驗「簡直像維多利亞時代」，並指出他在接受點滴治療時，被迫待在通風不良的走廊裡。當地衛生委員會對此致歉，承認他的遭遇未達國家醫療保健服務所追求的標準。

paragraphs.en: Data from the Welsh government shows why these changes are necessary. In the 2025-26 period, ambulances often faced long delays when arriving at hospitals, resulting in over 184,000 “lost hours.” Furthermore, thousands of patients who were ready to leave the hospital remained in beds because there was nowhere for them to go. This creates a “bottleneck”—a situation where the flow of patients stops moving—which forces new arrivals to wait in corridors or emergency rooms for much longer than is safe.
paragraphs.zh: 威爾斯政府的數據顯示了這些改革的必要性。在 2025 至 2026 年期間，救護車抵達醫院時常面臨嚴重延誤，導致超過 18 萬 4000 小時的「虛耗時間」。此外，數以千計已達出院標準的病患，因無處可去而持續佔用病床。這造成了「瓶頸」現象，即病患流動停滯，迫使新入院的病患必須在走廊或急診室等待遠超安全範圍的時間。

paragraphs.en: These delays have a high financial cost as well. Each hospital bed occupied by a patient who is medically ready to go home costs the NHS between £500 and £600 per day. In total, this inefficiency cost the system £172 million. Mabon ap Gwynfor, the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care, stated that the current situation is not consistent. He emphasized that when people need emergency help, they should receive it quickly and spend only as much time in the hospital as they truly need.
paragraphs.zh: 這些延誤也帶來高昂的財務成本。每張由已達出院標準的病患所佔用的病床，每天會讓國家醫療保健服務損失 500 至 600 英鎊。總計下來，這種效率低落的問題讓醫療體系損失了 1 億 7200 萬英鎊。威爾斯衛生與照護內閣部長馬邦·阿普·格溫福（Mabon ap Gwynfor）表示，目前的狀況並不一致。他強調，當民眾需要緊急救助時，應能迅速獲得協助，並僅在醫院停留真正必要的時長。

paragraphs.en: Medical professionals are calling for immediate action. Dr. Katja Empson, speaking for the Royal College of Emergency Medicine, warned that patients frequently face harm because they are being treated in unsafe spaces. She noted that the long waits are a reflection of pressures that exist across the entire care system, not just in one department. The government’s new plan aims to fix the “whole journey” of the patient, from the moment they call for help to the time they recover at home.
paragraphs.zh: 醫療專業人員正呼籲採取立即行動。代表皇家急診醫學學院（Royal College of Emergency Medicine）發言的卡蒂亞·艾普森醫師（Dr. Katja Empson）警告，病患常因在不安全的空間接受治療而受到傷害。她指出，漫長的等待反映了整個照護體系面臨的壓力，而非僅限於單一部門。政府的新計畫旨在改善病患的「全程旅程」，從他們撥打求救電話的那一刻起，直到康復返家為止。

paragraphs.en: As the NHS looks toward 2029, the focus remains on balancing the need for building repairs with the need to improve daily operations. Whether it is fixing maternity units or ensuring that patients in emergency rooms have a proper bed, the health service is under intense pressure to deliver better results. For patients like Mr. Railton, who has vowed never to return to the emergency department, the need for these improvements is not just a matter of policy—it is a matter of basic dignity and safety.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著國家醫療保健服務展望 2029 年，重點仍在於平衡建築修繕需求與改善日常營運。無論是修繕產科單位，還是確保急診室病患有合適的病床，醫療服務體系都承受著提供更好成果的巨大壓力。對於像瑞爾頓先生這樣發誓再也不回急診室的病患而言，這些改善需求不僅是政策問題，更是關乎基本尊嚴與安全的問題。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To reach or stretch across a certain area or range.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「延長時間」，這裡指問題的影響範圍擴大。文中：new reports highlight that the challenges extend deep into emergency care.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be of a lower standard or quality than what is expected or required.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由 fall 的過去式組成，指表現未達預期水準。文中：The local health board apologized, admitting that his experience fell below the standards the NHS aims to provide.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Time during which ambulances are unable to respond to new calls because they are waiting at hospitals.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 損失的工時（救護車無法出勤的時間）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡的「lost」並非指遺失，而是指因等待而浪費掉的時間。文中：In the 2025-26 period, ambulances often faced long delays when arriving at hospitals, resulting in over 184,000 “lost hours.”

keyTerms.definitionEn: Acting or done in the same way over time, especially so as to be fair or accurate.
keyTerms.noteZh: 在醫療語境下指服務品質不穩定，忽好忽壞。文中：Mabon ap Gwynfor, the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care, stated that the current situation is not consistent.

previousArticles.title: Safety Concerns Rise as Government Admits It Cannot Cost Maternity Repairs
previousArticles.summaryEn: The UK government is facing criticism for not knowing the cost of repairing failing maternity units. Nearly half of maternity and neonatal units in England currently fail to meet basic safety standards. Reports indicate that poor building conditions have interrupted clinical care thousands of times in recent years. Families and health officials have shared worrying stories about crumbling infrastructure and dangerous environments. The government is now under pressure to address these severe risks to mothers and babies.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary reason for the 'bottleneck' effect in Welsh hospitals?

options.A: Ambulances are arriving at hospitals more frequently than in previous years.
options.B: Patients who are medically fit to be discharged cannot leave due to a lack of onward care.
options.C: The government has reduced the number of available hospital beds to save money.
options.D: New patients are refusing to move from corridors into proper hospital rooms.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，文中明確提到「thousands of patients who were ready to leave the hospital remained in beds because there was nowhere for them to go. This creates a 'bottleneck'」，這直接解釋了阻塞效應的原因。選項 A 雖然提到救護車延誤，但並非造成阻塞的主因；選項 C 文章未提及減少床位；選項 D 則與事實不符，患者是被迫待在走廊，而非拒絕移動。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the state of the NHS?

options.A: The system's problems are limited to maternity and neonatal departments.
options.B: The government has successfully solved the issue of corridor care in Wales.
options.C: The challenges in the NHS are interconnected, affecting multiple stages of patient care.
options.D: The financial cost of the NHS is primarily due to building repairs rather than operational inefficiency.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第七段，Dr. Katja Empson 指出這些壓力存在於整個護理系統（across the entire care system），且政府的計畫旨在改善患者的「整個旅程」（whole journey）。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到問題也延伸至急診；選項 B 錯誤，因為計畫目標是在 2029 年前達成，目前尚未解決；選項 D 錯誤，文章提到床位佔用造成的低效率成本高達 1.72 億英鎊，這屬於營運問題。

quiz.question: In the context of the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'bottleneck' mean?

options.A: A situation that causes progress to slow down or stop.
options.B: A specific type of medical equipment used for emergency care.
options.C: A financial loss caused by poor management of hospital funds.
options.D: A physical storage area for hospital supplies and medicine.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中將「bottleneck」定義為「a situation where the flow of patients stops moving」，用來形容醫院因床位不足導致流程卡住的狀態。選項 B、C、D 皆與該詞在文中的比喻義完全無關，該詞在商業與管理語境中常用來形容導致進度停滯的瓶頸或障礙。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the NHS?

options.A: The NHS is primarily suffering from a lack of qualified medical staff.
options.B: Patients should avoid using NHS services until the government completes all building repairs.
options.C: The NHS is facing deep-rooted structural and operational challenges that require urgent, comprehensive reform.
options.D: The main focus of the NHS is to reduce the costs associated with hospital building maintenance.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文從產科設施問題、急診走廊醫療、患者經歷到系統性營運效率，全面探討了 NHS 面臨的困境，並強調需要採取行動來改善整個患者流程。選項 A 並非文章重點；選項 B 建議不合理；選項 D 片面強調維護成本，忽略了文章中同樣重要的醫療品質與患者尊嚴問題。
